subject: OpsWorks performance follow-up: capacity dimensioning & GPU tradeoffs
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Megan Liu <megan@opsworks.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: OpsWorks perf sync — post-demo recap & pilot asks

Hi Megan,

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate you and the engineering team walking through the traffic profile. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we scope the Dedicated pilot.

Summary of SLOs you called out (please correct me if I missed anything):
- P95 latency target: <= 200 ms for streaming responses up to 1k tokens (your internal goal was 150 ms — noted below).
- P99 latency target: <= 400 ms for worst-case under load.
- Sustained throughput: ~250 req/s (64-token average) with ability to burst to ~500 req/s for short windows (<= 5 minutes).
- Concurrency target: ~40 steady concurrent requests with spiky peaks.

What we attached:
- opsworks_requested_load.csv (the traffic sample you dropped on the call)
- opsworks_mutual_action_plan.docx (light mutual action plan template for the pilot)

Initial capacity / GPU tradeoff guidance (high level):
- H100 80GB: best raw inference throughput and lowest P95 in streaming-heavy workloads, especially for larger contexts; higher hourly cost but fewer nodes required for the same reserved throughput.
- A100 80GB: more cost-balanced option; slightly higher P95 latency than H100 in streaming, but often the sweet spot for mid-sized customers wanting predictability.
- A10G / T4-class: cost-effective for smaller models or customers who accept higher P95 and lower concurrency; not recommended if you need consistent sub-200ms P95 for 1k-token streams.

Proposed pilot plan (what we think will validate your SLOs):
1) 72-hour benchmark on Redwood Dedicated with two configurations: A100 slab and H100 slab.
2) Replay your attached traffic (we'll use opsworks_requested_load.csv) with streaming enabled, 1k token max, 95/99 latency capture, and KV cache warm-up.
3) Measure token/sec, P95/P99, and cost per 1M tokens; sample logs and traces will be available in the Console.

Immediate asks from OpsWorks to move forward:
- Confirm the P95 target (was 150 ms on your side, I recorded 200 ms in the call notes — please confirm).
- Confirm if pilot can run inside Redwood-managed Dedicated or if you require a VPC Private deployment (affects scheduling and access).
- Any compliance or data retention constraints for the pilot (syslog/audit retention windows).

Next steps I propose:
- OpsWorks: confirm P95/P99 targets and choose pilot hosting (Redwood Dedicated vs Private VPC).
- Redwood: stand up pilot slabs (A100 + H100) and share a short runbook + benchmark script.
- Joint: schedule a 30-min kickoff for the pilot next week.

I'll hold a matrix we can update with the actual measured numbers. If it helps, I've attached a preliminary capacity model (we'll refine with your traffic once we start the pilot).

Thanks,
David Kim
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0142
———
Attachments: opsworks_requested_load.csv (attachment), opsworks_mutual_action_plan.docx (attachment)
From: Megan Liu <megan@opsworks.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Tan <procurement@opsworks.com>, OpsWorks Engineering <eng@opsworks.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 17:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OpsWorks perf sync — post-demo recap & pilot asks

Hi David — thanks for the fast follow-up and the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Our internal goal is tighter: P95 <= 150 ms for typical conversational flows (64–256 token responses). The 200 ms you noted was our safe ceiling; we should target 150 ms and show headroom.
- P99 requirement: <= 400 ms, agreed.
- Sustained: we're planning for an initial target of 300 req/s (64-token average) with brief spikes to 600 req/s.
- We prefer Redwood-managed Dedicated for the pilot to keep onboarding friction low, but we need an option to move to VPC if procurement requires it.

Two asks for Redwood:
1) Can you provide a ballpark cost delta between A100 and H100 slabs for a 72-hour pilot (ballpark hourly + expected dedicated node count)?
2) Can you confirm whether your pilot can instrument P95/P99 traces and hand us the raw trace exports? We need them for our SRE post-mortem.

Cc'ing Sarah in procurement to keep them in the loop.

Thanks,
Megan Liu
Head of Platform, OpsWorks
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Megan Liu <megan@opsworks.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OpsWorks perf sync — post-demo recap & pilot asks

Megan — great, thanks for the clarifications. We can target 150 ms P95 as the goal for conversational flows. Below are concrete answers and a suggested pilot configuration.

Short answers:
- Raw traces: yes — we will export full traces (Console downloadable JSON) and sample token-level timing for your SRE team.
- Hosting: Redwood-managed Dedicated pilot is fine; if procurement later requires VPC, we can migrate but that adds ~3–5 business days to schedule.

Ballpark capacity / cost guidance (72-hour pilot):
- A100 slab (8x A100 80GB equivalent capacity in our Dedicated offering): expected steady throughput ~250–320 req/s (64-token avg) depending on model variant; estimated incremental pilot cost: ~$3,200–$4,500 for the 72h window (inclusive of reserved slab + telemetry).
- H100 slab (8x H100 80GB equiv): expected steady throughput ~420–500 req/s (64-token avg); estimated incremental pilot cost: ~$4,200–$6,000 for 72h.
- Approx delta: H100 ~25–35% higher cost for materially higher throughput and typically lower P95 in streaming flows.

Proposed pilot config (what we'll stand up):
- Two parallel slabs: 1x A100 slab, 1x H100 slab.
- Workload: replay opsworks_requested_load.csv with streaming turned on, 1k token max, client-concurrency sweep [20, 40, 80], collect P50/P95/P99 and tokens/sec.
- Acceptance gate: show that at your target concurrency (40) we meet P95 <= 150 ms on at least one slab; capture cost per 1M tokens for each slab.

Operational asks for scheduling:
- We need a 1-hr kickoff early next week to confirm test harness and confirm the model artifact (which model/quantization you expect to use).
- Please confirm if OpsWorks SRE needs any additional telemetry (e.g., raw token timestamps / full traces).

I'll attach a quick capacity model and the benchmark script we'll run so you can review.

If this looks good, I'll loop our performance team to provision the slabs and schedule the kickoff.

Best,
David
———
Attachments: capacity_model_v1.xlsx, gpu_benchmark_script.sh
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Megan Liu <megan@opsworks.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Mar 2028 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: OpsWorks perf sync — pilot picks and runbook (internal)

Hannah / Karthik — forwarding OpsWorks thread. They confirmed 150 ms P95 target and asked for a Redwood-managed Dedicated pilot (72h) with A100 and H100 slabs. Key asks: raw traces, token-level timing, and a concurrency sweep at [20,40,80].

My asks for you both:
- Hannah: can you please provision two pilot slabs for next Tue (A100 slab + H100 slab) and reserve them for 72 hours? Also, tag them with the deal id DW-2028-OPS-003 and ensure telemetry export is enabled.
- Karthik: can you run a quick sanity run with our internal micro-bench (gpu_benchmark_script.sh) to validate the expected per-node tokens/sec on our internal H100 and A100 testbeds? Capture P95 for 1k token streaming and push results to the OpsWorks folder (link below).

I've attached our capacity model v1 — update the expected node counts if your bench numbers differ. We'll use these to provide a short cost delta for procurement.

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/opsworks-pilot

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick sync if helpful.

-David
